findings.finding: The initial receipt check incorrectly treated the canonical blueprint object digest as identical to the pretty-printed artifact byte digest.
findings.resolution: Preserve both digests and verify intent-to-object plus object-to-exact-file lineage through verifyReceiptArtifacts().

findings.finding: Generic recursive cleanup was broader than the composer's exact two-file ownership model.
findings.resolution: Cleanup now refuses unexpected entries, unlinks only the two owned filenames, and removes only the validated new root.

findings.finding: The consent envelope declares public instruction data, but the composer cannot determine whether human-entered text is actually public.
findings.resolution: Receipt truth keeps declaredDataClassContentVerified false and documentation requires the trusted host to exclude private material.

findings.finding: The first CLI draft ran immediately when required, complicating safe static reuse and parser tests.
findings.resolution: Execution is now guarded by require.main and parsing/run functions are exported.

findings.finding: Composer input bytes, output files, output bytes, and operation count can be enforced; future candidate duration and memory cannot be enforced without a runtime.
findings.resolution: The receipt separates enforced composer observations from false durationEnforced and memoryEnforced claims.

findings.finding: The composer validates and derives a specification, but it does not implement the declared transformation or generate executable code.
findings.resolution: Keep desired outcomes UNPROVEN and type creation.blueprint-to-code.provider as missing.

findings.finding: The exact acknowledgement is replayable and proves neither identity nor informed understanding, trusted time, or live revocation.
findings.resolution: Keep all corresponding receipt truth fields false and require a later authenticated host decision contract.
